decisions.reason: As an award-backed yogurt variant close to the core range, it has shown positive market promise and is inexpensive to keep while demand becomes clearer.
Because management presented it as a flagship product and it fits the established cheese business, the option value of continuing clearly exceeds the small cost of staying in market.
This semi-hard cheese is close to existing capabilities and customers, so despite limited evidence so far it is still worth keeping open for another selling period.
The spicy cheese line offers several variants and learning opportunities within the firm's core category, making continued market presence more valuable than early abandonment.
The mild creamy soft cheese broadens the assortment in a familiar segment, and with only short time on the market there is still enough uncertainty to justify waiting.

Washed-rind soft cheese is a narrower taste profile and therefore more exposed to pruning, but it remains close enough to the firm's competencies that management would likely give it more time before dropping it.
